title: Jenne-jeno (Djenne-Djenno)
summary: Jenne-jeno, on the floodplain of the Inland Niger Delta in Mali, is one of the longest-occupied Iron Age sites in West Africa, with a sequence from about 250 BCE to 1400 CE. At its height it may have held around 20,000 people and traded in iron ore, copper and pottery. It was largely abandoned in the 14th century, after nearby Djenné had replaced it as a trade centre.

uncertainty.note: Occupation sequence 250 BC-1400 AD per the excavation record; World History Encyclopedia says it flourished to c. 1100 and was all but abandoned in the 14th century. 250 BCE is year -249.

as_recorded.value: The Jenne-jeno sequence spans roughly 250 B.C. to 1400 A.D.
all but abandoned for unknown reasons in the 14th century CE
